answer: The economy spends reputation the way a market spends money: sparingly and against verified performance, so Sybil inflation is filtered out before it can compound into a decisive advantage. The defense holds because trust accrues slowly and is lost fast, so a farm that ever submits a copied answer destroys the value of that identity. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a garden as the anchor of the cost.
